_comment: Cross-implementation parity corpus for fixture-shape detection, the one copy both suites read: the tester's tests/test_fixture_shape_parity.py and the platform web app's fixture-shape parity test. The Python module (services/otelcol-testing/app/fixture_shape.py) and the web app's module are hand-kept mirrors; this corpus is the contract that catches drift. If you change detection rules, advisory message text, or strategy-picking in one module, update the other AND this file — a stale entry fails on both sides at once. Inputs are plain UTF-8 text (truncation/BOM/binary edge cases live in each suite's own unit tests, since they aren't expressible as small shared strings). The target_strategies cases carry the run's target pipeline too (`target_pipeline`, a key of the text's service.pipelines, or a stale name, which falls back to the signal's pipelines).

detection.name: raw_lines
detection.text:
2026-05-26 INFO order placed
2026-05-26 WARN payment declined

advisories.name: raw_lines_otlp
advisories.expected_message: Your fixture looks like raw text log lines, but the target pipeline uses an OTLP receiver. The sandbox OTLP/HTTP endpoint will reject each line as invalid JSON, so the run is likely to produce no output. Convert the fixture to OTLP-JSON to test this pipeline, or test a `file_log` (or `filelog`) receiver pipeline against this fixture as-is.

advisories.name: ndjson_otlp
advisories.expected_message: Your fixture is NDJSON, but the target pipeline uses an OTLP receiver. Each line is POSTed to the sandbox OTLP/HTTP endpoint and will be rejected unless every line is itself a valid OTLP document (a JSON object containing `resourceLogs`, `resourceMetrics`, or `resourceSpans`). If these are app log records, run the test on a `file_log` (or `filelog`) pipeline with a `json_parser` operator instead.

advisories.name: logs_fixture_traces_pipeline
advisories.expected_message: Your fixture contains OTLP logs data, but the target pipeline handles traces. The sandbox POSTs the fixture to the OTLP/HTTP traces endpoint, which decodes logs data as zero traces records — so the run is likely to produce no output. Select a traces fixture (an OTLP envelope with `resourceSpans`), or run this fixture against a logs pipeline.

advisories.name: metrics_fixture_logs_pipeline
advisories.expected_message: Your fixture contains OTLP metrics data, but the target pipeline handles logs. The sandbox POSTs the fixture to the OTLP/HTTP logs endpoint, which decodes metrics data as zero logs records — so the run is likely to produce no output. Select a logs fixture (an OTLP envelope with `resourceLogs`), or run this fixture against a metrics pipeline.

advisories.name: traces_array_metrics_pipeline
advisories.expected_message: Your fixture contains OTLP traces data, but the target pipeline handles metrics. The sandbox POSTs the fixture to the OTLP/HTTP metrics endpoint, which decodes traces data as zero metrics records — so the run is likely to produce no output. Select a metrics fixture (an OTLP envelope with `resourceMetrics`), or run this fixture against a traces pipeline.

advisories.name: envelope_filelog
advisories.expected_message: Your fixture looks like an OTLP-JSON envelope, but the target pipeline uses a `file_log` (or `filelog`) receiver. `file_log` reads input line by line, so the whole envelope arrives as a single record with the raw JSON string in `body` — your operator chain runs against that one line, not the records nested inside. To test the records as OTLP, run on an otlp-receiver pipeline. To test `file_log` operators, supply a fixture with one log per line.

strategies.name: filelog_wired_to_logs
strategies.yaml:
receivers:
  filelog:
    include: [/var/log/x.log]
service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [filelog]
      exporters: [debug]

strategies.name: syslog_wired_to_logs
strategies.yaml:
receivers:
  syslog:
    tcp:
      listen_address: 0.0.0.0:514
    protocol: rfc5424
service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [syslog]
      exporters: [debug]
